content.title: About
content.content: Vegetable curry is a fragrant dish made from a mix of vegetables, tomato base, coconut milk, and classic Indian spices such as turmeric, cumin, coriander and garam masala. It is rich in vitamins, minerals and plant protein, making it suitable for vegetarians and vegans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Curry originates from South Asian cuisine but now has countless regional variations.
Coconut milk softens the heat of the spices and gives the dish a creamy texture.
Vegetable curry can be adapted to seasonal produce: broccoli, cauliflower, bell pepper, carrot or pumpkin.
Traditionally it is served with basmati rice or naan flatbread.
The spices used in curry possess antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The vegetables and spices provide B6 and folate, supporting metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber from the vegetables aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant spices
items.content: Turmeric and coriander contain curcumin and other compounds that combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Cumin and paprika may help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: When prepared with a modest amount of oil or coconut milk, the dish remains heart‑friendly.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to turmeric, cumin or coriander.

items.title: Heat level
items.content: Excessive chili can cause stomach irritation in sensitive people.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain salt; monitor added salt to keep sodium intake moderate.

items.title: Coconut milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to coconut should substitute with another plant‑based milk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot vegetable curry with steamed rice, quinoa or whole‑grain flatbreads. Garnish with fresh cilantro, a squeeze of lime, or a dollop of yogurt for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the cooked curry to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. Reheat on the stove or in a microwave, adding a splash of water or coconut milk to restore its creamy consistency.
